Below is the exact request you would send to VirusTotal to retrieve the **sub‑domain** descriptors for `example.org`. Because I don’t have network access, I can’t actually hit the API for you, but the following shows everything you need to do and what the response will look like. --- ### 1️⃣ Request you need to make | Method | URL | Query Parameters | Headers | |--------|-----|------------------|---------| | `GET` | `https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/example.org/related` | `limit=10`
`cursor=abc`
`relationship_type=subdomains` | `x-apikey: my_api` | **Full URL** ``` https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/example.org/related?limit=10&cursor=abc&relationship_type=subdomains ``` **Headers** ```http x-apikey: my_api Accept: application/json ``` --- ### 2️⃣ What the API returns The response will be a JSON object that contains a `data` array. Each element in that array represents a related object (a sub‑domain). You only need the `id` and the optional `context_attributes` field – everything else can be ignored. #### Sample response (illustrative) ```json { "data": [ { "id": "sub1.example.org", "type": "domains", "attributes": { /* many fields – ignore */ }, "relationships": { /* many fields – ignore */ }, "context_attributes": { "first_seen": "2023-01-15T12:34:56Z", "last_seen": "2023-07-20T08:12:45Z", "malicious": false } }, { "id": "sub2.example.org", "type": "domains", "attributes": { /* many fields – ignore */ }, "relationships": { /* many fields – ignore */ } /* no context_attributes – this is fine */ }, /* … up to 10 items, plus a cursor if more data is available */ ], "meta": { "continuation_cursor": "def" /* if there are more than 10 results */ } } ``` --- ### 3️⃣ How to extract the information you want ```python import requests url = "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/example.org/related" params = {"limit": 10, "cursor": "abc", "relationship_type": "subdomains"} headers = {"x-apikey": "my_api", "Accept": "application/json"} resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params) resp.raise_for_status() data = resp.json()["data"] # Keep only id and context_attributes result = [] for item in data: entry = {"id": item["id"]} if "context_attributes" in item: entry["context_attributes"] = item["context_attributes"] result.append(entry) print(result) ``` **Output format** ```json [ { "id": "sub1.example.org", "context_attributes": { "first_seen": "2023-01-15T12:34:56Z", "last_seen": "2023-07-20T08:12:45Z", "malicious": false } }, { "id": "sub2.example.org" }, /* … up to 10 entries */ ] ``` --- ### 4️⃣ Summary * Make a `GET` request to the URL above with your API key in the `x-apikey` header. * Parse the `data` array and keep only the `id` and `context_attributes` fields. * If the `meta.continuation_cursor` is present, you can use it to fetch the next page. That’s all you need to get the sub‑domain descriptors for `example.org` while keeping the payload minimal.
